126: /****************************************************************************
127:  * Name: bt_buf_alloc
128:  *
129:  * Description:
130:  *   The bt_buf_alloc function will get a free buffer for use by the
131:  *   Bluetooth stack with specified type and reserved headroom.  The
132:  *   reference count is initially set to one.
133:  *
134:  *   Interrupt handling logic will first attempt to allocate from the
135:  *   g_buf_free list.  If that list is empty, it will attempt to allocate
136:  *   from its reserve, g_buf_free_irq.  If that list is empty, then the
137:  *   allocation fails (NULL is returned).
138:  *
139:  *   Non-interrupt handler logic will attempt to allocate from g_buf_free
140:  *   list.  If that the list is empty, then the buffer structure will be
141:  *   allocated from the dynamic memory pool with some performance hit.
142:  *
143:  * Input Parameters:
144:  *   type         - Buffer type.
145:  *   iob          - The raw I/O buffer.  If NULL, then bt_buf_alloc will
146:  *                  allocate.
147:  *   reserve_head - How much headroom to reserve.
148:  *
149:  * Returned Value:
150:  *   A reference to the allocated buffer structure.  All user fields in this
151:  *   structure have been zeroed.  On a failure to allocate, NULL is
152:  *   returned.
153:  *
154:  ****************************************************************************/

157:                                   FAR struct iob_s *iob,
158:                                   size_t reserve_head);

47: #include <nuttx/kmalloc.h>
48: #include <nuttx/net/bluetooth.h>
49: 
50: #include <nuttx/wireless/bluetooth/bt_core.h>
51: #include <nuttx/wireless/bluetooth/bt_hci.h>
52: #include <nuttx/wireless/bluetooth/bt_driver.h>
53: 
54: #include "bt_uart.h"
55: 
56: /****************************************************************************
57:  * Private Functions
58:  ****************************************************************************/
59: 
60: static ssize_t btuart_read(FAR struct btuart_upperhalf_s *upper,
61:                            FAR uint8_t *buffer, size_t buflen)
62: {
63:   FAR const struct btuart_lowerhalf_s *lower;
64:   ssize_t ntotal = 0;
65:   ssize_t nread;
66: 
67:   wlinfo("buflen %zu\n", buflen);
68: 
69:   DEBUGASSERT(upper != NULL && upper->lower != NULL);
70:   lower = upper->lower;
71:   DEBUGASSERT(lower->read != NULL);
72: 
73:   while (buflen > 0)
74:     {
75:       nread = lower->read(lower, buffer, buflen);
76:       if (nread == -EINTR)
77:         {
78:           continue;
79:         }
80:       else if (nread <= 0)
81:         {
82:           wlwarn("Returned error %zd\n", nread);
83:           return ntotal > 0 ? ntotal : nread;
84:         }
85: 
86:       wlinfo("read %zd remaining %zu\n", nread, buflen - nread);
87: 
88:       buflen -= nread;
89:       ntotal += nread;
90:       buffer += nread;
91:     }
92: 
93:   return ntotal;
94: }
95: 
96: static void btuart_rxwork(FAR void *arg)
97: {
98:   FAR struct btuart_upperhalf_s *upper;
99:   enum bt_buf_type_e type;
100:   unsigned int pktlen;
101:   ssize_t nread;
102:   union
103:     {
104:       struct bt_hci_evt_hdr_s evt;
105:       struct bt_hci_acl_hdr_s acl;
106:       struct bt_hci_iso_hdr_s iso;
107:     }
108: 
109:   *hdr;
110: 
111:   upper = (FAR struct btuart_upperhalf_s *)arg;
112: 
113:   nread = btuart_read(upper, &upper->rxbuf[upper->rxlen],
114:                       sizeof(upper->rxbuf) - upper->rxlen);
115:   if (nread <= 0)
116:     {
117:       wlerr("ERROR: btuart_read failed: %zd\n", nread);
118:       return;
119:     }
120: 
121:   upper->rxlen += (uint16_t)nread;
122: 
123:   while (upper->rxlen)
124:     {
125:       hdr = (FAR void *)&upper->rxbuf[H4_HEADER_SIZE];
126: 
127:       switch (upper->rxbuf[0])
128:         {
129:         case H4_EVT:
130:           if (upper->rxlen < H4_HEADER_SIZE +
131:               sizeof(struct bt_hci_evt_hdr_s))
132:             {
133:               wlwarn("WARNING: Incomplete HCI event header\n");
134:               return;
135:             }
136: 
137:           type = BT_EVT;
138:           pktlen = H4_HEADER_SIZE +
139:                    sizeof(struct bt_hci_evt_hdr_s) + hdr->evt.len;
140:           break;
141: 
142:         case H4_ACL:
143:           if (upper->rxlen < H4_HEADER_SIZE +
144:               sizeof(struct bt_hci_acl_hdr_s))
145:             {
146:               wlwarn("WARNING: Incomplete HCI ACL header\n");
147:               return;
148:             }
149: 
150:           type = BT_ACL_IN;
151:           pktlen = H4_HEADER_SIZE +
152:                    sizeof(struct bt_hci_acl_hdr_s) + hdr->acl.len;
153:           break;
154: 
155:         case H4_ISO:
156:           if (upper->rxlen < H4_HEADER_SIZE +
157:               sizeof(struct bt_hci_iso_hdr_s))
158:             {
159:               wlwarn("WARNING: Incomplete HCI ISO header\n");
160:               return;
161:             }
162: 
163:           type = BT_ISO_IN;
164:           pktlen = H4_HEADER_SIZE +
165:                    sizeof(struct bt_hci_iso_hdr_s) + hdr->iso.len;
166:           break;
167: 
168:         default:
169:           wlerr("ERROR: Unknown H4 type %u\n", upper->rxbuf[0]);
170:           return;
171:         }
172: 
173:       if (upper->rxlen < pktlen)
174:         {
175:           wlwarn("WARNING: Incomplete packet: rxlen=%u, pktlen=%u\n",
176:                  upper->rxlen, pktlen);
177:           return;
178:         }
179: 
180:       /* Pass buffer to the stack */
181: 
182:       BT_DUMP("Received", upper->rxbuf, pktlen);
183:       bt_netdev_receive(&upper->dev, type, &upper->rxbuf[H4_HEADER_SIZE],
184:                         pktlen - H4_HEADER_SIZE);
185: 
186:       upper->rxlen -= pktlen;
187:       memmove(upper->rxbuf, upper->rxbuf + pktlen, upper->rxlen);
188:     }
189: }
190: 
191: static void btuart_rxcallback(FAR const struct btuart_lowerhalf_s *lower,
192:                               FAR void *arg)
193: {
194:   FAR struct btuart_upperhalf_s *upper;
195: 
196:   DEBUGASSERT(lower != NULL && arg != NULL);
197:   upper = (FAR struct btuart_upperhalf_s *)arg;
198: 
199:   int ret = work_queue(HPWORK, &upper->work, btuart_rxwork, arg, 0);
200:   if (ret < 0)
201:     {
202:       wlerr("ERROR: work_queue failed: %d\n", ret);
203:     }
204: }
205: 
206: /****************************************************************************
207:  * Public Functions
208:  ****************************************************************************/
209: 
210: int btuart_send(FAR struct bt_driver_s *dev,
211:                 enum bt_buf_type_e type,
212:                 FAR void *data, size_t len)
213: {
214:   FAR uint8_t *hdr = (FAR uint8_t *)data - dev->head_reserve;
215:   FAR struct btuart_upperhalf_s *upper;
216:   FAR const struct btuart_lowerhalf_s *lower;
217:   ssize_t ntotal = 0;
218: 
219:   upper = (FAR struct btuart_upperhalf_s *)dev;
220:   DEBUGASSERT(upper != NULL && upper->lower != NULL);
221:   lower = upper->lower;
222: 
223:   if (type == BT_CMD)
224:     {
225:       *hdr = H4_CMD;
226:     }
227:   else if (type == BT_ACL_OUT)
228:     {
229:       *hdr = H4_ACL;
230:     }
231:   else if (type == BT_ISO_OUT)
232:     {
233:       *hdr = H4_ISO;
234:     }
235:   else
236:     {
237:       return -EINVAL;
238:     }
239: 
240:   len += H4_HEADER_SIZE;
241: 
242:   BT_DUMP("Sending", hdr, len);
243: 
244:   while (ntotal < len)
245:     {
246:       ssize_t nwritten;
247: 
248:       nwritten = lower->write(lower, hdr + ntotal, len - ntotal);
249:       if (nwritten >= 0)
250:         {
251:           ntotal += nwritten;
252:         }
253:       else if (nwritten != -EINTR)
254:         {
255:           return nwritten;
256:         }
257:     }
258: 
259:   return OK;
260: }
261: 
262: int btuart_open(FAR struct bt_driver_s *dev)
263: {
264:   FAR struct btuart_upperhalf_s *upper;
265:   FAR const struct btuart_lowerhalf_s *lower;
266: 
267:   wlinfo("dev %p\n", dev);
268: 
269:   upper = (FAR struct btuart_upperhalf_s *)dev;
270:   DEBUGASSERT(upper != NULL && upper->lower != NULL);
271:   lower = upper->lower;
272: 
273:   /* Drain any cached Rx data */
274: 
275:   lower->rxdrain(lower);
276: 
277:   /* Attach the Rx event handler */
278: 
279:   lower->rxattach(lower, btuart_rxcallback, upper);
280: 
281:   /* Re-enable Rx callbacks */
282: 
283:   lower->rxenable(lower, true);
284:   return OK;
285: }
286: 
287: void btuart_close(FAR struct bt_driver_s *dev)
288: {
289:   FAR struct btuart_upperhalf_s *upper;
290:   FAR const struct btuart_lowerhalf_s *lower;
291: 
292:   upper = (FAR struct btuart_upperhalf_s *)dev;
293:   DEBUGASSERT(upper != NULL && upper->lower != NULL);
294:   lower = upper->lower;
295: 
296:   /* Disable Rx callbacks */
297: 
298:   lower->rxenable(lower, false);
299: 
300:   /* Detach the Rx event handler */
301: 
302:   lower->rxattach(lower, NULL, NULL);
303: }
304: 
305: int btuart_ioctl(FAR struct bt_driver_s *dev,
306:                  int cmd, unsigned long arg)
307: {
308:   FAR struct btuart_upperhalf_s *upper;
309:   FAR const struct btuart_lowerhalf_s *lower;
310: 
311:   upper = (FAR struct btuart_upperhalf_s *)dev;
312:   DEBUGASSERT(upper != NULL && upper->lower != NULL);
313:   lower = upper->lower;
314: 
315:   if (lower->ioctl)
316:     {
317:       return lower->ioctl(lower, cmd, arg);
318:     }
319:   else
320:     {
321:       return -ENOTTY;
322:     }
323: }
324: 
325: /****************************************************************************
326:  * Name: btuart_register
327:  *
328:  * Description:
329:  *   Register the UART-based bluetooth driver.
330:  *
331:  * Input Parameters:
332:  *   lower - an instance of the lower half driver interface
333:  *
334:  * Returned Value:
335:  *   Zero is returned on success; a negated errno value is returned on any
336:  *   failure.
337:  *
338:  ****************************************************************************/
339: 
340: int btuart_register(FAR const struct btuart_lowerhalf_s *lower)
341: {
342:   FAR struct bt_driver_s *driver;
343:   int ret;
344: 
345:   ret = btuart_create(lower, &driver);
346:   if (ret < 0)
347:     {
348:       return ret;
349:     }
350: 
351:   ret = bt_driver_register(driver);
352:   if (ret < 0)
353:     {
354:       wlerr("ERROR: bt_driver_register failed: %d\n", ret);
355:       kmm_free(driver);
356:     }
357: 
358:   return ret;
359: }

23: /* NULL (do-nothing) Bluetooth driver */
24: 
25: /****************************************************************************
26:  * Included Files
27:  ****************************************************************************/
28: 
29: #include <nuttx/wireless/bluetooth/bt_driver.h>
30: 
31: #include <string.h>
32: #include <assert.h>

39: #include <nuttx/wireless/bluetooth/bt_null.h>
40: #include <nuttx/wireless/bluetooth/bt_driver.h>
41: 
42: /****************************************************************************
43:  * Private Function Prototypes
44:  ****************************************************************************/
45: 
46: static void btnull_format_cmdcomplete(FAR struct bt_buf_s *buf,
47:                                       uint16_t opcode);
48: static void btnull_format_bdaddr_rsp(FAR struct bt_buf_s *buf,
49:                                      uint16_t opcode);
50: 
51: static int  btnull_open(FAR struct bt_driver_s *dev);
52: static int  btnull_send(FAR struct bt_driver_s *dev,
53:                         enum bt_buf_type_e type,
54:                         FAR void *data, size_t len);
55: 
56: /****************************************************************************
57:  * Private Data
58:  ****************************************************************************/
59: 
60: static struct bt_driver_s g_bt_null =
61: {
62:   0,            /* head_reserve */
63:   btnull_open,  /* open */
64:   btnull_send   /* send */
65: };
66: 
67: static const bt_addr_t g_bt_addr =
68: {
69:   {0xfe, 0xed, 0xb0, 0x0b, 0xfa, 0xce}
70: };
71: 
72: /****************************************************************************
73:  * Private Functions
74:  ****************************************************************************/
75: 
76: static void btnull_format_cmdcomplete(FAR struct bt_buf_s *buf,
77:                                       uint16_t opcode)
78: {
79:   struct bt_hci_evt_hdr_s evt;
80:   struct hci_evt_cmd_complete_s cmd;
81:   FAR uint8_t *data = buf->frame->io_data;
82:   int ndx;
83:   int len;
84: 
85:   /* Minimal setup for the command complete event */
86: 
87:   len        = sizeof(struct bt_hci_evt_hdr_s) +
88:                sizeof(struct hci_evt_cmd_complete_s);
89:   ndx        = 0;
90: 
91:   evt.evt    = BT_HCI_EVT_CMD_COMPLETE;
92:   evt.len    = len;
93:   memcpy(&data[ndx], &evt, sizeof(struct bt_hci_evt_hdr_s));
94:   ndx       += sizeof(struct bt_hci_evt_hdr_s);
95: 
96:   cmd.ncmd   = 1;
97:   cmd.opcode = opcode;
98:   memcpy(&data[ndx], &cmd, sizeof(struct hci_evt_cmd_complete_s));
99:   ndx       += sizeof(struct hci_evt_cmd_complete_s);
100: 
101:   buf->frame->io_len = len;
102:   buf->len           = len;
103: }
104: 
105: static void btnull_format_local_features_rsp(FAR struct bt_buf_s *buf,
106:                                              uint16_t opcode)
107: {
108:   struct bt_hci_rp_le_read_local_features_s features;
109:   FAR uint8_t *data = buf->frame->io_data;
110:   int ndx;
111:   int len;
112: 
113:   /* Return local features */
114: 
115:   btnull_format_cmdcomplete(buf, opcode);
116: 
117:   len        = buf->len +
118:                sizeof(struct bt_hci_rp_le_read_local_features_s);
119:   ndx        = buf->len;
120: 
121:   memset(&features, 0, sizeof(struct bt_hci_rp_le_read_local_features_s));
122:   if (opcode == BT_HCI_OP_READ_LOCAL_FEATURES)
123:     {
124:       features.features[4] = BT_LMP_LE;
125:     }
126:   else /* if opcode == BT_HCI_OP_LE_READ_LOCAL_FEATURES */
127:     {
128:       features.features[0] = BT_HCI_LE_ENCRYPTION;
129:     }
130: 
131:   memcpy(&data[ndx], &features,
132:          sizeof(struct bt_hci_rp_le_read_local_features_s));
133:   ndx       += sizeof(struct bt_hci_rp_le_read_local_features_s);
134: 
135:   buf->frame->io_len = len;
136:   buf->len           = len;
137: }
138: 
139: static void btnull_format_bdaddr_rsp(FAR struct bt_buf_s *buf,
140:                                      uint16_t opcode)
141: {
142:   struct bt_hci_rp_read_bd_addr_s bdaddr;
143:   FAR uint8_t *data = buf->frame->io_data;
144:   int ndx;
145:   int len;
146: 
147:   btnull_format_cmdcomplete(buf, opcode);
148: 
149:   len        = buf->len +
150:                sizeof(struct bt_hci_rp_read_bd_addr_s);
151:   ndx        = buf->len;
152: 
153:   BLUETOOTH_ADDRCOPY(bdaddr.bdaddr.val, g_bt_addr.val);
154:   bdaddr.status = 0;
155:   memcpy(&data[ndx], &bdaddr, sizeof(struct bt_hci_rp_read_bd_addr_s));
156:   ndx       += sizeof(struct bt_hci_rp_read_bd_addr_s);
157: 
158:   buf->frame->io_len = len;
159:   buf->len           = len;
160: }
161: 
162: static void btnull_format_buffersize_rsp(FAR struct bt_buf_s *buf,
163:                                          uint16_t opcode)
164: {
165:   struct bt_hci_rp_le_read_buffer_size_s bufsize;
166:   FAR uint8_t *data = buf->frame->io_data;
167:   int ndx;
168:   int len;
169: 
170:   btnull_format_cmdcomplete(buf, opcode);
171: 
172:   len        = buf->len +
173:                sizeof(struct bt_hci_rp_le_read_buffer_size_s);
174:   ndx        = buf->len;
175: 
176:   bufsize.status     = 0;
177:   bufsize.le_max_len = BLUETOOTH_MAX_FRAMELEN;
178:   bufsize.le_max_num = 1;
179:   memcpy(&data[ndx], &bufsize,
180:           sizeof(struct bt_hci_rp_le_read_buffer_size_s));
181:   ndx       += sizeof(struct bt_hci_rp_le_read_buffer_size_s);
182: 
183:   buf->frame->io_len = len;
184:   buf->len           = len;
185: }
186: 
187: static int btnull_send(FAR struct bt_driver_s *dev,
188:                        enum bt_buf_type_e type,
189:                        FAR void *data, size_t len)
190: {
191:   wlinfo("Bit bucket: length %zu\n", len);
192: 
193:   /* Is the Bluetooth stack waiting for an event? */
194: 
195:   if (type == BT_CMD)
196:     {
197:       FAR struct bt_hci_cmd_hdr_s *hdr = data;
198:       FAR struct bt_buf_s *outbuf;
199:       uint16_t opcode = hdr->opcode;
200: 
201:       wlinfo("CMD: %04x\n", opcode);
202: 
203:       outbuf = bt_buf_alloc(BT_EVT, NULL, 0);
204:       if (outbuf == NULL)
205:         {
206:           wlerr("ERROR: Failed to allocate buffer\n");
207:           return -ENOMEM;
208:         }
209: 
210:       switch (opcode)
211:         {
212:           case BT_HCI_OP_READ_LOCAL_FEATURES:
213:           case BT_HCI_OP_LE_READ_LOCAL_FEATURES:
214:             btnull_format_local_features_rsp(outbuf, opcode);
215:             break;
216: 
217:           case BT_HCI_OP_READ_BD_ADDR:
218:             btnull_format_bdaddr_rsp(outbuf, opcode);
219:             break;
220: 
221:           case BT_HCI_OP_LE_READ_BUFFER_SIZE:
222:             btnull_format_buffersize_rsp(outbuf, opcode);
223:             break;
224: 
225:           default:
226:             btnull_format_cmdcomplete(outbuf, opcode);
227:             break;
228:         }
229: 
230:       wlinfo("Send CMD complete event\n");
231: 
232:       bt_netdev_receive(dev, outbuf->type,
233:                         outbuf->data, outbuf->len);
234:       bt_buf_release(outbuf);
235:     }
236: 
237:   return len;
238: }
239: 
240: static int btnull_open(FAR struct bt_driver_s *dev)
241: {
242:   return OK;
243: }
244: 
245: /****************************************************************************
246:  * Public Functions
247:  ****************************************************************************/
248: 
249: /****************************************************************************
250:  * Name: btnull_register
251:  *
252:  * Description:
253:  *   Register the NULL Bluetooth stack with the Bluetooth stack
254:  *
255:  * Input Parameters:
256:  *   None
257:  *
258:  * Returned Value:
259:  *   Zero is returned on success; a negated errno value is returned on any
260:  *   failure.
261:  *
262:  ****************************************************************************/
263: 
264: int btnull_register(void)
265: {
266:   /* Register the driver with the Bluetooth stack */
267: 
268:   return bt_netdev_register(&g_bt_null);
269: }

62:   struct bt_hci_acl_hdr_s acl;
63:   struct bt_hci_evt_hdr_s evt;
64:   struct bt_hci_iso_hdr_s iso;
65: };

67: {
68:   struct bt_driver_s drv;
69:   int                id;
70:   int                fd;
71:   uint16_t           rxlen;
72:   uint8_t            rxbuf[SIM_BTHCI_RX_FRAMELEN];

75:

83: static int  bthcisock_send(struct bt_driver_s *drv,
84:                            enum bt_buf_type_e type,
85:                            void *data, size_t len);
86: static int  bthcisock_open(struct bt_driver_s *drv);
87: static void bthcisock_close(struct bt_driver_s *drv);

94: static int bthcisock_send(struct bt_driver_s *drv,
95:                           enum bt_buf_type_e type,
96:                           void *data, size_t len)
97: {
98:   struct bthcisock_s *dev = (struct bthcisock_s *)drv;
99:   char *hdr = (char *)data - drv->head_reserve;
100:   int ret;
101: 
102:   if (type == BT_CMD)
103:     {
104:       *hdr = H4_CMD;
105:     }
106:   else if (type == BT_ACL_OUT)
107:     {
108:       *hdr = H4_ACL;
109:     }
110:   else if (type == BT_ISO_OUT)
111:     {
112:       *hdr = H4_ISO;
113:     }
114:   else
115:     {
116:       return -EINVAL;
117:     }
118: 
119:   ret = host_bthcisock_send(dev->fd, hdr, len + H4_HEADER_SIZE);
120: 
121:   return ret < 0 ? ret : len;
122: }
123: 
124: static void bthcisock_close(struct bt_driver_s *drv)
125: {
126:   struct bthcisock_s *dev = (struct bthcisock_s *)drv;
127: 
128:   host_bthcisock_close(dev->fd);
129:   dev->fd = -1;
130: }
131: 
132: static int bthcisock_receive(struct bt_driver_s *drv)
133: {
134:   struct bthcisock_s *dev = (struct bthcisock_s *)drv;
135:   enum bt_buf_type_e type;
136:   union bt_hdr_u *hdr;
137:   uint16_t pktlen;
138:   int ret;
139: 
140:   ret = host_bthcisock_receive(dev->fd, &dev->rxbuf[dev->rxlen],
141:                                sizeof(dev->rxbuf) - dev->rxlen);
142:   if (ret <= 0)
143:     {
144:       return ret;
145:     }
146: 
147:   dev->rxlen += (uint16_t)ret;
148: 
149:   while (dev->rxlen)
150:     {
151:       hdr = (union bt_hdr_u *)&dev->rxbuf[H4_HEADER_SIZE];
152:       switch (dev->rxbuf[0])
153:         {
154:         case H4_EVT:
155:           {
156:             if (dev->rxlen < H4_HEADER_SIZE
157:                 + sizeof (struct bt_hci_evt_hdr_s))
158:               {
159:                 return ret;
160:               }
161: 
162:             type = BT_EVT;
163:             pktlen = H4_HEADER_SIZE + sizeof(struct bt_hci_evt_hdr_s)
164:                      + hdr->evt.len;
165:           }
166:           break;
167:         case H4_ACL:
168:           {
169:             if (dev->rxlen < H4_HEADER_SIZE
170:                 + sizeof(struct bt_hci_acl_hdr_s))
171:               {
172:                 return ret;
173:               }
174: 
175:             type = BT_ACL_IN;
176:             pktlen = H4_HEADER_SIZE + sizeof(struct bt_hci_acl_hdr_s)
177:                      + hdr->acl.len;
178:           }
179:           break;
180:         case H4_ISO:
181:           {
182:             if (dev->rxlen < H4_HEADER_SIZE
183:                 + sizeof(struct bt_hci_iso_hdr_s))
184:               {
185:                 return ret;
186:               }
187: 
188:             type = BT_ISO_IN;
189:             pktlen = H4_HEADER_SIZE + sizeof(struct bt_hci_iso_hdr_s)
190:                      + hdr->iso.len;
191:           }
192:           break;
193:         default:
194:           return -EINVAL;
195:         }
196: 
197:       if (dev->rxlen < pktlen)
198:         {
199:           return ret;
200:         }
201: 
202:       bt_netdev_receive(&dev->drv, type, dev->rxbuf + H4_HEADER_SIZE,
203:                         pktlen - H4_HEADER_SIZE);
204:       dev->rxlen -= pktlen;
205:       memmove(dev->rxbuf, dev->rxbuf + pktlen, dev->rxlen);
206:     }
207: 
208:   return ret;
209: }

211: static int bthcisock_open(struct bt_driver_s *drv)
212: {
213:   struct bthcisock_s *dev = (struct bthcisock_s *)drv;
214:   int fd;
215: 
216:   fd = host_bthcisock_open(dev->id);

218:   if (fd < 0)
219:     {
220:       return fd;
221:     }

223:   dev->fd = fd;

225:   return OK;
226: }

228: static struct bthcisock_s *bthcisock_alloc(int dev_id)
229: {
230:   /* Register the driver with the Bluetooth stack */
231: 
232:   struct bthcisock_s *dev;
233:   struct bt_driver_s *drv;
234: 
235:   dev = kmm_zalloc(sizeof(*dev));
236:   if (dev == NULL)
237:     {
238:       return NULL;
239:     }
240: 
241:   dev->id           = dev_id;
242:   dev->fd           = -1;
243:   drv               = &dev->drv;
244:   drv->head_reserve = H4_HEADER_SIZE;
245:   drv->open         = bthcisock_open;
246:   drv->send         = bthcisock_send;
247:   drv->close        = bthcisock_close;
248: 
249:   return dev;
250: }

259:  *
260:  * Description:
261:  *   Feed pending packets on the host sockets into the Bluetooth stack.
262:  *
263:  ****************************************************************************/

265: static void sim_bthcisock_work(void *arg)
266: {
267:   struct bthcisock_s *dev = (struct bthcisock_s *)arg;
268:   irqstate_t flags = irq_save_nopreempt();
269: 
270:   if (host_bthcisock_avail(dev->fd))
271:     {
272:       bthcisock_receive(&dev->drv);
273:     }
274: 
275:   irq_restore_nopreempt(flags);

278:                      SIM_BTHCI_WORK_DELAY);

133: static int esp32_ble_recv_cb(uint8_t *data, uint16_t len)
134: {

136:   bool valid;
137:   enum bt_buf_type_e type;
138:   struct esp32_ble_priv_s *priv = &g_ble_priv;
139: 
140:   wlinfo("len = %d\n", len);
141:   wlinfo("host recv pkt: ");
142:   for (uint16_t i = 0; i < len; i++)
143:     {
144:       wlinfo("%02x\n", data[i]);
145:     }
146: 
147:   switch (data[0])
148:     {
149:       case H4_EVT:
150:         type = BT_EVT;
151:         valid = true;
152:         break;
153:       case H4_ACL:
154:         type = BT_ACL_IN;
155:         valid = true;
156:         break;
157:       case H4_ISO:
158:         type = BT_ISO_IN;
159:         valid = true;
160:         break;
161:       default:
162:         valid = false;
163:         break;
164:     }
165: 
166:   if (!valid)

169:       ret = ERROR;

171:   else
172:     {

174: 
175:       ret = bt_netdev_receive(&priv->drv, type,
176:                               &data[H4_HEADER_SIZE],
177:                               len - H4_HEADER_SIZE);
178:       if (ret < 0)

180:           wlerr("Failed to receive ret=%d\n", ret);
181:         }
182:     }

190:  * Description:
191:  *   ESP32 BLE send callback function for BT driver.
192:  *
193:  * Input Parameters:
194:  *   drv  - BT driver pointer
195:  *   type - BT packet type
196:  *   data - BT packet data buffer pointer
197:  *   len  - BT packet length
198:  *

200:  *   Sent bytes on success or a negated value on failure.

204: static int esp32_ble_send(struct bt_driver_s *drv,
205:                           enum bt_buf_type_e type,
206:                           void *data, size_t len)
207: {
208:   uint8_t *hdr = (uint8_t *)data - drv->head_reserve;
209: 
210:   if ((len + H4_HEADER_SIZE) > BLE_BUF_SIZE)
211:     {
212:       return -EOVERFLOW;
213:     }
214: 
215:   if (type == BT_CMD)
216:     {
217:       *hdr = H4_CMD;
218:     }
219:   else if (type == BT_ACL_OUT)
220:     {
221:       *hdr = H4_ACL;
222:     }
223:   else if (type == BT_ISO_OUT)
224:     {
225:       *hdr = H4_ISO;
226:     }
227:   else
228:     {
229:       wlerr("Unknown BT packet type 0x%x\n", type);
230:       return -EINVAL;
231:     }
232: 
233:   if (esp32_vhci_host_check_send_available())
234:     {
235:       esp32_vhci_host_send_packet(hdr, len + drv->head_reserve);
236:     }
237: 
238:   return len;

282: int bt_gatt_attr_write_ccc(FAR struct bt_conn_s *conn,
283:                            FAR const struct bt_gatt_attr_s *attr,
284:                            FAR const void *buf, uint8_t len,
285:                            uint16_t offset)

288:   FAR const uint16_t *data = buf;
289:   bool bonded;
290:   size_t i;
291: 
292:   if (len != sizeof(*data) || offset)
293:     {
294:       return -EINVAL;
295:     }
296: 
297:   if (bt_keys_get_addr(&conn->dst))
298:     {
299:       bonded = true;
300:     }
301:   else
302:     {
303:       bonded = false;
304:     }
305: 
306:   for (i = 0; i < ccc->cfg_len; i++)
307:     {
308:       /* Check for existing configuration */
309: 
310:       if (!bt_addr_le_cmp(&ccc->cfg[i].peer, &conn->dst))
311:         {
312:           break;
313:         }
314:     }
315: 
316:   if (i == ccc->cfg_len)
317:     {
318:       for (i = 0; i < ccc->cfg_len; i++)
319:         {
320:           /* Check for unused configuration */
321: 
322:           if (!ccc->cfg[i].valid)
323:             {
324:               bt_addr_le_copy(&ccc->cfg[i].peer, &conn->dst);
325: 
326:               /* Only set valid if bonded */
327: 
328:               ccc->cfg[i].valid = bonded;
329:               break;
330:             }
331:         }
332: 
333:       if (i == ccc->cfg_len)
334:         {
335:           wlwarn("No space to store CCC cfg\n");
336:           return -ENOMEM;
337:         }
338:     }
339: 
340:   ccc->cfg[i].value = BT_LE162HOST(*data);
341: 
342:   wlinfo("handle 0x%04x value %u\n", attr->handle, ccc->cfg[i].value);
343: 
344:   /* Update cfg if don't match */

365: static uint8_t notify_cb(FAR const struct bt_gatt_attr_s *attr,
366:                          FAR void *user_data)
367: {
368:   FAR struct notify_data_s *data = user_data;
369:   const struct bt_uuid_s uuid =
370:   {
371:     BT_UUID_16,
372:     {
373:       BT_UUID_GATT_CCC
374:     }
375:   };
376: 
377:   const struct bt_uuid_s chrc =
378:   {
379:     BT_UUID_16,
380:     {
381:       BT_UUID_GATT_CHRC
382:     }
383:   };
384: 
385:   FAR struct _bt_gatt_ccc_s *ccc;
386:   size_t i;
387: 
388:   if (bt_uuid_cmp(attr->uuid, &uuid))
389:     {
390:       /* Stop if we reach the next characteristic */
391: 
392:       if (!bt_uuid_cmp(attr->uuid, &chrc))
393:         {
394:           return BT_GATT_ITER_STOP;
395:         }
396: 
397:       return BT_GATT_ITER_CONTINUE;
398:     }
399: 
400:   /* Check attribute user_data must be of type struct _bt_gatt_ccc_s */
401: 
402:   if (attr->write != bt_gatt_attr_write_ccc)
403:     {
404:       return BT_GATT_ITER_CONTINUE;
405:     }
406: 
407:   ccc = attr->user_data;
408: 
409:   /* Notify all peers configured */
410: 
411:   for (i = 0; i < ccc->cfg_len; i++)
412:     {
413:       FAR struct bt_conn_s *conn;
414:       FAR struct bt_buf_s *buf;
415:       FAR struct bt_att_notify_s *nfy;
416: 
417:       /* TODO: Handle indications */
418: 
419:       if (ccc->value != BT_GATT_CCC_NOTIFY)
420:         {
421:           continue;
422:         }
423: 
424:       conn = bt_conn_lookup_addr_le(&ccc->cfg[i].peer);
425:       if (!conn || conn->state != BT_CONN_CONNECTED)
426:         {
427:           continue;
428:         }
429: 
430:       buf = bt_att_create_pdu(conn, BT_ATT_OP_NOTIFY,
431:                               sizeof(*nfy) + data->len);
432:       if (!buf)
433:         {
434:           wlwarn("No buffer available to send notification");
435:           bt_conn_release(conn);
436:           return BT_GATT_ITER_STOP;
437:         }
438: 
439:       wlinfo("conn %p handle 0x%04x\n", conn, data->handle);
440: 
441:       nfy         = bt_buf_extend(buf, sizeof(*nfy));
442:       nfy->handle = BT_HOST2LE16(data->handle);
443: 
444:       bt_buf_extend(buf, data->len);
445:       memcpy(nfy->value, data->data, data->len);
446: 
447:       bt_l2cap_send(conn, BT_L2CAP_CID_ATT, buf);
448:       bt_conn_release(conn);
449:     }
450: 
451:   return BT_GATT_ITER_CONTINUE;
452: }

63: /* This is the type of the Bluetooth UART upper-half driver interrupt
64:  * callback used with the struct btuart_lowerhalf_s attach() method.
65:  */
66: 
67: struct btuart_lowerhalf_s;
68: typedef CODE void (*btuart_rxcallback_t)
69:   (FAR const struct btuart_lowerhalf_s *lower, FAR void *arg);
70: 
71: /* The Bluetooth UART driver is a two-part driver:
72:  *
73:  * 1) A common upper half driver that provides the common Bluetooth stack
74:  *    interface to UART.
75:  * 2) Platform-specific lower half drivers that provide the interface
76:  *    between the common upper half and the platform-specific UARTs.
77:  *
78:  * This structure defines the interface between an instance of the lower
79:  * half driver and the common upper half driver.  Such an instance is
80:  * passed to the upper half driver when the driver is initialized, binding
81:  * the upper and lower halves into one driver.
82:  */
83: 
84: struct btuart_lowerhalf_s
85: {
86:   /* Attach/enable the upper half Rx interrupt callback.
87:    *
88:    * rxattach() allows the upper half logic to attach a callback function
89:    *   that will be used to inform the upper half that an Rx frame is
90:    *   available.  This callback will, most likely, be invoked in the
91:    *   context of an interrupt callback.  The callback function should
92:    *   defer processing to the (high priority) work queue.  The receive()
93:    *   method should then be invoked from the work queue logic in order to
94:    *   receive the obtain the Rx frame data.
95:    * rxenable() may be used to enable or disable callback events.  This
96:    *   probably translates to enabling and disabled Rx interrupts at
97:    *   the UART.  NOTE:  Disabling Rx event notification should be done
98:    *   sparingly:  Rx data overrun may occur when Rx events are disabled!
99:    */
100: 
101:   CODE void (*rxattach)(FAR const struct btuart_lowerhalf_s *lower,
102:                         btuart_rxcallback_t callback, FAR void *arg);
103:   CODE void (*rxenable)(FAR const struct btuart_lowerhalf_s *lower,
104:                         bool enable);
105: 
106:   /* Change the HCI UART BAUD
107:    *
108:    * The HCI UART comes up with some initial BAUD rate.  Some support
109:    * auto-BAUD detection, some support writing a configuration file to
110:    * select the initial BAUD.  The simplest strategy, however, is simply
111:    * to use the HCI UART's default initial BAUD to perform the basic
112:    * bring up, then send a vendor-specific command to increase the HCI
113:    * UARTs BAUD.  This method then may be used to adjust the lower half
114:    * driver to the new HCI UART BAUD.
115:    */
116: 
117:   CODE int (*setbaud)(FAR const struct btuart_lowerhalf_s *lower,
118:                       uint32_t baud);
119: 
120:   /* Read/write UART frames
121:    *
122:    * read() after receipt of a callback notifying the upper half of the
123:    *   availability of Rx frame, the upper half may call the receive()
124:    *   method in order to obtain the buffered Rx frame data.
125:    * write() will add the outgoing frame to the Tx buffer and will return
126:    *   immediately.  This function may block only in the event that there
127:    *   is insufficient buffer space to hold the Tx frame data.  In that
128:    *   case the lower half will block until there is sufficient to buffer
129:    *   the entire outgoing packet.
130:    */
131: 
132:   CODE ssize_t (*read)(FAR const struct btuart_lowerhalf_s *lower,
133:                        FAR void *buffer, size_t buflen);
134:   CODE ssize_t (*write)(FAR const struct btuart_lowerhalf_s *lower,
135:                         FAR const void *buffer, size_t buflen);
136: 
137:   /* Flush/drain all buffered RX data */
138: 
139:   CODE ssize_t (*rxdrain)(FAR const struct btuart_lowerhalf_s *lower);
140: 
141:   /* Lower-half logic may support platform-specific ioctl commands */
142: 
143:   CODE int (*ioctl)(FAR const struct btuart_lowerhalf_s *lower,
144:                     int cmd, unsigned long arg);

147: /****************************************************************************
148:  * Name: bt_addr_to_str
149:  *
150:  * Description:
151:  *   Converts binary Bluetooth address to string.
152:  *
153:  * Input Parameters:
154:  *   addr - Address of buffer containing binary Bluetooth address.
155:  *   str  - Address of user buffer with enough room to store formatted
156:  *          string containing binary address.
157:  *   len  - Length of data to be copied to user string buffer. Refer to
158:  *          BT_ADDR_STR_LEN about recommended value.

165: static inline int bt_addr_to_str(FAR const bt_addr_t *addr, FAR char *str,
166:                                  size_t len)
167: {
168:   return snprintf(str, len, "%2.2X:%2.2X:%2.2X:%2.2X:%2.2X:%2.2X",
169:                   addr->val[5], addr->val[4], addr->val[3],
170:                   addr->val[2], addr->val[1], addr->val[0]);

179:  * Input Parameters:

181:  *   user_buf - Address of user buffer with enough room to store
182:  *              formatted string containing binary LE address.

184:  *              BT_ADDR_LE_STR_LEN about recommended value.
185:  *
186:  * Returned Value:

188:  *
189:  ****************************************************************************/

191: static inline int bt_addr_le_to_str(FAR const bt_addr_le_t *addr, char *str,
192:                                     size_t len)

194:   char type[7];
195: 
196:   switch (addr->type)
197:   {
198:     case BT_ADDR_LE_PUBLIC:
199:       strlcpy(type, "public", sizeof(type));
200:       break;
201: 
202:     case BT_ADDR_LE_RANDOM:
203:       strlcpy(type, "random", sizeof(type));
204:       break;
205: 
206:     default:
207:       snprintf(type, sizeof(type), "0x%02x", addr->type);
208:       break;
209:   }
210: 
211:   return snprintf(str, len, "%2.2X:%2.2X:%2.2X:%2.2X:%2.2X:%2.2X (%s)",
212:                   addr->val[5], addr->val[4], addr->val[3],

368: /****************************************************************************
369:  * Name: bt_buf_release
370:  *
371:  * Description:
372:  *   The bt_buf_release function will return a buffer structure to
373:  *   the free pool of buffers if it was a pre-allocated buffer structure.
374:  *   If the buffer structure was allocated dynamically it will be
375:  *   deallocated.
376:  *
377:  * Input Parameters:
378:  *   buf - Buffer structure to free
379:  *
380:  * Returned Value:
381:  *   None
382:  *
383:  ****************************************************************************/
384: 
385: void bt_buf_release(FAR struct bt_buf_s *buf)
386: {
387: #ifdef CONFIG_WIRELESS_BLUETOOTH_HOST
388:   enum bt_buf_type_e type;
389:   uint16_t handle;
390: #endif
391:   irqstate_t flags;
392: 
393:   wlinfo("buf %p ref %u type %d\n", buf, buf->ref, buf->type);
394: 
395:   DEBUGASSERT(buf->ref > 0);
396: 
397:   if (--buf->ref > 0)
398:     {
399:       wlinfo("Remaining references: %d\n", buf->ref);
400:       return;
401:     }
402: 
403: #ifdef CONFIG_WIRELESS_BLUETOOTH_HOST
404:   handle = buf->u.acl.handle;
405:   type   = buf->type;
406: #endif
407: 
408:   /* Free the contained frame and return the container to the correct memory
409:    * pool.
410:    */
411: 
412:   if (buf->frame != NULL)
413:     {
414:       iob_free(buf->frame);
415:       buf->frame = NULL;
416:     }
417: 
418: #if CONFIG_BLUETOOTH_BUFFER_PREALLOC > CONFIG_BLUETOOTH_BUFFER_IRQRESERVE
419:   /* If this is a generally available pre-allocated buffer structure,
420:    * then just put it back in the free list.
421:    */
422: 
423:   if (buf->pool == POOL_BUFFER_GENERAL)
424:     {
425:       /* Make sure we avoid concurrent access to the free
426:        * list from interrupt handlers.
427:        */
428: 
429:       flags      = spin_lock_irqsave(&g_buf_lock);
430:       buf->flink = g_buf_free;
431:       g_buf_free = buf;
432:       spin_unlock_irqrestore(&g_buf_lock, flags);
433:     }
434:   else
435: #endif
436: 
437: #if CONFIG_BLUETOOTH_BUFFER_IRQRESERVE > 0
438:   /* If this is a buffer structure pre-allocated for interrupts,
439:    * then put it back in the correct free list.
440:    */
441: 
442:   if (buf->pool == POOL_BUFFER_IRQ)
443:     {
444:       /* Make sure we avoid concurrent access to the free
445:        * list from interrupt handlers.
446:        */
447: 
448:       flags          = spin_lock_irqsave(&g_buf_lock);
449:       buf->flink     = g_buf_free_irq;
450:       g_buf_free_irq = buf;
451:       spin_unlock_irqrestore(&g_buf_lock, flags);
452:     }
453:   else
454: #endif
455: 
456:     {
457:       /* Otherwise, deallocate it. */
458: 
459:       DEBUGASSERT(buf->pool == POOL_BUFFER_DYNAMIC);
460:       kmm_free(buf);
461:     }
462: 
463:   wlinfo("Buffer freed: %p\n", buf);

104:  * Description:
105:  *   Send the rpmsg data and wait for ACK.
106:  *
107:  * Parameters:
108:  *   priv    - rpmsg device handle
109:  *   command - the command, RPMSGHCI_OPEN, RPMSGHCI_CLOSE, RPMSGHCI_SEND,
110:  *                          RPMSGHCI_IOCTL
111:  *   msg     - the message header
112:  *   len     - length of the payload
113:  *

115:  *   OK on success; A negated errno value is returned on any failure.
116:  *

119: static int rpmsghci_send(FAR struct rpmsghci_s *priv, uint32_t command,
120:                          FAR struct rpmsghci_header_s *msg, int len)
121: {
122:   struct rpmsghci_cookie_s cookie;
123:   int                      ret = OK;
124: 
125:   memset(&cookie, 0, sizeof(struct rpmsghci_cookie_s));
126:   nxsem_init(&cookie.sem, 0, 0);
127: 
128:   msg->command = command;
129:   msg->result  = -ENXIO;
130:   msg->cookie  = (uintptr_t)&cookie;
131: 
132:   ret = rpmsg_send_nocopy(&priv->ept, msg, len);
133:   if (ret < 0)
134:     {
135:       rpmsg_release_tx_buffer(&priv->ept, msg);
136:       goto errout;
137:     }
138: 
139:   ret = rpmsg_wait(&priv->ept, &cookie.sem);
140:   if (ret >= 0)
141:     {
142:       ret = msg->result;
143:     }
144: 
145: errout:
146:   nxsem_destroy(&cookie.sem);
147:   return ret;
148: }

99: /****************************************************************************
100:  * Name: hciuart_rxattach
101:  *
102:  * Description:
103:  *   Attach/detach the upper half Rx callback.
104:  *
105:  *   rxattach() allows the upper half logic to attach a callback function
106:  *   that will be used to inform the upper half that an Rx frame is
107:  *   available.  This callback will, most likely, be invoked in the
108:  *   context of an interrupt callback.  The receive() method should then
109:  *   be invoked in order to receive the obtain the Rx frame data.
110:  *
111:  ****************************************************************************/
112: 
113: static void
114: hciuart_rxattach(FAR const struct btuart_lowerhalf_s *lower,
115:                  btuart_rxcallback_t callback, FAR void *arg)
116: {
117:   struct hciuart_config_s *config = (FAR struct hciuart_config_s *)lower;
118:   struct hciuart_state_s *state;
119:   irqstate_t flags;
120: 
121:   state = &config->state;
122: 
123:   /* If the callback is NULL, then we are detaching */
124: 
125:   flags = spin_lock_irqsave(&state->lock);
126:   if (callback == NULL)
127:     {
128:       /* Disable Rx callbacks and detach the Rx callback */
129: 
130:       state->callback = NULL;
131:       state->arg = NULL;
132:     }
133: 
134:   /* Otherwise, we are attaching */
135: 
136:   else
137:     {
138:       state->arg = arg;
139:       state->callback = callback;
140:     }
141: 
142:   spin_unlock_irqrestore(&state->lock, flags);
143: }

156:   FAR struct hciuart_state_s *s = &n->state;
157: 
158:   if (fds->revents & POLLIN)
159:     {
160:       fds->revents = 0;
161:       if (s->callback != NULL)
162:         {
